title: Parasyte
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Worm-like Parasites arrive on Earth and take over human brains, then feed on other humans. One fails to reach 17-year-old Shinichi Izumi's brain and instead takes over his right hand, becoming Migi; the two keep separate minds and must cooperate to survive attacks from other Parasites. The series uses this to ask what makes us human and whether humanity has any right to moral superiority over other species.
life_message: It holds up compassion and the bonds of love as what make us human, while questioning human arrogance toward nature.

delivery.evidence: Thompson (ANN House of 1000 Manga): an environmental tale whose message is mostly implied; values questions over answers.

personified.ideology: cold self-interest that cannot grasp self-sacrifice
a Parasyte trying to understand humans as a collective

delivery.note: Its questions about humanity's place in nature are raised through the Parasytes' behavior more than speeches.

winners_losers: Shinichi survives and keeps his humanity, but at great cost, and Parasites like Goto are destroyed. The story extends sympathy to both humans and Parasites and is critical of human arrogance toward nature.
